messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — GPU hotpool saturation detected (us-west-2). Queue depth spiking, 429s increasing. Pager sent to #oncall. https://status.redwood.example/incident/3939991234 :rotating_light:
jamie.sre: seeing it in dashboards, hotpath GPUs at 98-100% for last 4m. queue_depth => 12.4k,  p95 latency climbing.
oncall-bot: paging @olivia.oncall :bell: (escalation policy: critical)
olivia.oncall: on it. joining voice. taking ownership for initial triage.
jamie.sre: quick context — started ~7m ago after a traffic surge from a partner batch job. Autoscaler not adding healthy hotpath pods despite CPU/GPU demand.
will.platform: grabbing logs from autoscaler controller. suspect quota/limit or scale-lock.
maria.ml: from model-side metrics, KV cache hit-rate dropped; many warmup requests hitting full model, increasing GPU memory pressure.
ashley.ops: customer-impact: synthetic probes show 7.1% 429s, top-5 orgs impacted, two paying customers hitting higher error rates. CS notified.
cs-alex: notified customer success and opened support tickets for the two customers. We'll provide ETA once we have a mitigation.
jamie.sre: commands I'm running: ```
# queue snapshot
redwood monitor query --metric queue_depth --env prod --window 5m --pool hotpath
# autoscaler status
kubectl -n redwood get hpa hotpath-autoscaler -o yaml
```
jamie.sre: output (trimmed): ```
queue_depth: 12400
hotpath_gpu_util: 98.6%
hotpath_autoscaler:
  currentReplicas: 20
  desiredReplicas: 42
  maxReplicas: 20
```
jamie.sre: autoscaler desired > max => stuck due to maxReplica cap at 20. also tokenbucket logs show hotpath refill_rate ~= 100 req/s (should be 1000) — tier policy misapplied during yesterday's rollout.
will.platform: confirmed HPA maxReplicas=20 in config map `autoscale-policies/prod-hotpath`. that rollout from last night accidentally set `maxReplicas` to the test value.
maria.ml: model fallback config is live — we can route non-urgent requests to gpt-medium or gpt-small to reduce GPU pressure if we flip the route for lower-priority traffic.
olivia.oncall: mitigation plan: 1) bump maxReplicas to 60 (temp), 2) patch tokenbucket refill for hotpath tier to 1200, 3) enable emergency routing for non-critical traffic to smaller model. apply one at a time and watch queue.
jamie.sre: executing step 1 now: `kubectl patch hpa hotpath-autoscaler -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":60}}' -n redwood`
jamie.sre: patch applied. HPA reconciled. desired=42 -> scaling up to 42 then to new desired if load persists.
will.platform: autoscaler logs show scale events queued. starting node provisioning. cloud provider ETA ~90s per node, ramping.
ashley.ops: applying tokenbucket patch as step 2: `redwood config set tokenbucket.hotpath.refill_rate 1200 --env prod` (dry-run first)
maria.ml: we should also temporarily lower `min_preferred_model` for internal traffic to gpt-medium via route override to immediately reduce per-request GPU footprint.
olivia.oncall: doing route override for non-authenticated traffic: `redwood routes override --route /api/generate --pool hotpath --model gpt-medium --percentage 40`
olivia.oncall: override applied — 40% of new requests now go to gpt-medium. monitoring.
incident-bot: ALERT — 429 rate dropped from 7.1% -> 3.8% in 2m after overrides :thumbsup:
jamie.sre: autoscaler finished adding replicas; hotpath pods = 45, GPU util dropped to ~75%. queue_depth down to 3.2k. latency p95 improving.
will.platform: tokenbucket refill applied (confirmed). old config: `refill_rate: 100` new: `refill_rate: 1200`. previous misconfig was unintentionally shipping test values during a config promotion.
cs-alex: customer update: preliminary mitigation in place, asked CS to send interim note. customers A and B acknowledged — waiting on full postmortem.
maria.ml: important: model cache warmup still causing transient spikes; recommend priming caches once scale stabilizes. scheduling a short background priming job.
ashley.ops: short-term mitigation done. now tracking for rollback window. if stable for 30m, we'll keep adjusted values and start post-incident cleanup.
olivia.oncall: impact summary: - Duration (major): ~7m from detection to control; extended tail for backpressure ~25m. - Peak affected request rate: 7.1% 429s -> reduced to <1% now. - Customers with elevated errors: 2 high-priority orgs (support tickets open).
jamie.sre: root cause (initial hypothesis): config promotion from staging to prod accidentally included test autoscale caps + tokenbucket test refill. those combined with a traffic surge caused desiredReplicas > maxReplicas and tokenbucket throttling causing rapid 429s and queue growth.
will.platform: immediate follow-ups (owners): - revert staging-to-prod config pipeline to prevent caps (will.platform) - enforce validation test that checks maxReplicas >= desiredReplicas under recent load (jamie.sre) - add tokenbucket schema validation on deploys (maria.ml)
olivia.oncall: runbook note: add a simple emergency command to increase maxReplicas for HPA and override tokenbucket refill for hotpath. documented steps and CLI snippets added to runbook.
cs-alex: CS will follow up with impacted customers with timeline and postmortem link once published.
jamie.sre: creating incident ticket and tagging for postmortem: `INC-2026-394` (placeholder).
incident-bot: incident annotated: severity: high, owner: olivia.oncall, mitigation: autoscaler cap bump + tokenbucket fix + route override, status: mitigated->monitoring.
olivia.oncall: monitoring for 40m. if stable, I'll start coordinated rollback of route overrides and reduce temporary maxReplicas to normal baseline during maintenance window.
jamie.sre: note for postmortem: capture the partner batch job pattern, add traffic spike guardrails (burst policies), and harden pipeline so only validated autoscale values can be promoted.
maria.ml: will schedule a cache-priming job and evaluate whether model sharding could reduce memory pressure long-term.
ashley.ops: action items assigned in tracker. I'll open the accelerate change request for the HPA default to be 100 max with safety checks.
olivia.oncall: thanks team — great response. leaving @will.platform and @jamie.sre to follow up on infra fixes. I'll hand off monitoring to next oncall in 40m unless anything regresses.
cs-alex: will update customers in 30m with status.
jamie.sre: final note before handoff: total mitigation time to steady state ~12m, customer error rates returned to acceptable levels. postmortem owner: jamie.sre.
olivia.oncall: handing off to next oncall now. :white_check_mark:
